title_candidates: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe cleans up speech as you dictate
Gemini's new transcription model turns rough speech into clean text
summary: Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe cleans up speech as it becomes text, supports 85+ languages in APIs, and now powers English dictation in Gemini for macOS.

primary_source.title: Intelligent transcription with Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
primary_source.author: Diego Melendo Casado and Luke Leonhard, on behalf of the Gemini Audio Team
key_facts: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe turns speech into polished, formatted text while handling background noise, specialized terms, filler words, and mid-sentence corrections.
Google offers one model for bidirectional live streaming and another for recorded audio with speaker labels and word-level timestamps.
The model automatically detects more than 85 languages and can recognize supplied custom vocabulary, including specialized terms and unusual spellings.
Google reports average word error rates of 4.0% for streaming and 2.6% for non-streaming transcription, based on measurements from Artificial Analysis.
Google says the time required to finalize a transcript improved by 70% compared with Chirp 3, again citing Artificial Analysis measurements.
Consumer access includes English intelligent dictation in the Gemini app for macOS and Rambler on Android in selected countries and languages; Chrome support is planned.
The macOS experience places cleaned text at the cursor and can optionally use screen context for tasks beyond dictation.
Developer access is available through Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, while enterprise access is available through Google's enterprise agent platform.

quote_candidates.text: our most precise speech-to-text model yet, designed for intelligent voice interactions.

supporting_sources.title: Gemini for macOS adds new natural language capabilities
key_facts: Long-pressing the Fn key lets a user dictate into the active Mac window, and releasing the key inserts cleaned text at the cursor.
Intelligent dictation is the default; a separate reasoning option can use screen context for editing, summarizing, or image tasks.
Google says the voice capability is rolling out globally to Gemini for macOS users in English.

supporting_sources.title: Gemini Audio - AI transcription
key_facts: The official model page lists support for pre-recorded transcription in more than 85 languages, custom vocabulary, timestamps, and speaker attribution.
Google AI Studio links directly to both the recorded-audio and live transcription interfaces.

supporting_sources.title: Gemini Apps Privacy Hub
key_facts: Speak to Window captures microphone audio together with the active window so Gemini can understand the request.
Google says instruction transcripts follow the user's Keep Activity setting, while the audio itself is not stored.

prerequisites: An Apple silicon Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.0 or later
A Google Account and access to the Gemini app for macOS
English speech and a harmless sentence of your own to dictate

steps.instruction: Open gemini.google/mac, download Gemini for macOS, move it into Applications, open it, and sign in; stop if the app is unavailable for your device, account, or region.

Read the Speak to Window section of the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub: it sends microphone audio and the active window to Gemini, saves transcripts according to Keep Activity, and does not store the audio; stop if that handling is unsuitable for your test.
In Gemini, open Settings > Speak to Window and leave reasoning off so this test only dictates and cleans text; then open a blank TextEdit document and close or deselect private material.
Place the cursor in TextEdit, hold Fn, speak one harmless English sentence with an 'um' or a mid-sentence correction, then release Fn; verify that cleaned, formatted text appears at the cursor.

Compare the inserted text with what you said and correct names, numbers, or missing words before using it; press Escape to cancel and stop if Speak to Window is missing, transcription fails, or the app unexpectedly requests payment.

risk_flags: The general-user guide is limited to the documented macOS experience: Apple silicon, macOS 15 or later, English, and feature rollout availability.
The broader 85-language claim applies to the transcription models and APIs; the macOS Speak to Window rollout is English-only at publication time.
Speak to Window can send active-window context with microphone audio, so the guide keeps reasoning off and uses a blank non-sensitive document.
Official pages differ on preview versus general-availability wording for developer endpoints; the article avoids making an access-status claim beyond named surfaces.
